title: Chapter 40 — Midnight, Forecastle
paragraphs: HARPOONERS AND SAILORS.
(The foresail rises and reveals the watch standing, lounging, leaning, and lying in various positions, all singing in chorus.)
Farewell and goodbye to you, Spanish ladies! Farewell and goodbye to you, ladies of Spain! Our captain's commanded —
1ST NANTUCKET SAILOR. Oh, boys, don't be sentimental — it's bad for the digestion! Have a drink, follow me!
(Sings, and all follow.)

Our captain stood upon the deck, a spyglass in his hand, surveying all those splendid whales that spouted near the strand. Oh, your tubs in your boats, my boys, and by your braces stand, and we'll take one of those fine whales, hand, boys, over hand! So be cheerful, my lads! May your hearts never fail! While the bold harpooner is striking the whale!
MATE'S VOICE FROM THE QUARTER-DECK. Eight bells there, forward!

2ND NANTUCKET SAILOR. Stop the singing! Eight bells! Do you hear, bell-boy? Strike the bell eight, Pip, you little rascal! And let me call the watch. I've got the right kind of mouth for that — a barrel-sized mouth. So, so — (Thrusts his head down the hatch.) Starboard watch, ahoy! Eight bells down below! Get up!

DUTCH SAILOR. Great sleeping tonight, mate — a fat night for it. I credit our old sultan's wine for that. It puts some to sleep as much as it livens up others. We sing, they sleep — yes, lying down there like barrels in a cellar. At them again! Here, take this copper tube and shout through it. Tell them to stop dreaming about their girls. Tell them it's Judgment Day — they've got to kiss their sweethearts goodbye and face the reckoning. That's the way — that's it! Your throat hasn't been ruined by eating Amsterdam butter.

FRENCH SAILOR. Listen, boys! Let's have a jig or two before we anchor in Blanket Bay. What do you say? Here comes the other watch. Everybody on your feet! Pip! Little Pip! Come on with your tambourine!
PIP. (Sulky and sleepy.) Don't know where it is.

FRENCH SAILOR. Beat your belly, then, and flap your ears. Dance, men, I say! Merry's the word — hurrah! Damn me, won't you dance? Line up, single file, and gallop into the double-shuffle! Throw yourselves into it! Legs! Legs!
ICELAND SAILOR. I don't like your dance floor, mate — it's too springy for my taste. I'm used to ice. Sorry to dampen the mood, but excuse me.
MALTESE SAILOR. Me too. Where are your girls? Who but a fool would take his own left hand in his right and say, 'How do you do?' Partners! I need partners!
SICILIAN SAILOR. That's right — girls and a green lawn! Then I'll dance with you — yes, I'll leap like a grasshopper!
LONG-ISLAND SAILOR. Well, well, you grumblers, there's plenty of us willing. Make hay while you can, I say. All legs go to the harvest soon enough. Ah! Here comes the music — now we're in business!

AZORE SAILOR. (Climbing up and tossing the tambourine through the hatch.) Here you go, Pip — and there's the windlass post. Climb up! Now, boys! (Half of them dance to the tambourine; some go below; some sleep or lie among the coils of rigging. Plenty of cursing.)
AZORE SAILOR. (Dancing.) Go, Pip! Bang it, bell-boy! Rig it, dig it, jig it, bell-boy! Make sparks fly! Break those jinglers!
PIP. Jinglers, you say? There goes another one — fell off. I'm pounding it too hard.
CHINA SAILOR. Rattle your teeth, then, and keep pounding — make a pagoda of yourself.
FRENCH SAILOR. Wild and merry! Hold up your hoop, Pip, so I can jump through it! Rip the sails! Tear loose!
TASHTEGO. (Quietly smoking.) That's a white man for you. He calls that fun. Humph! I'll save my sweat.

OLD MANX SAILOR. I wonder whether those cheerful lads realize what they're dancing over. 'I'll dance on your grave' — that's the bitterest curse of your night-witches, those who beat headwinds round corners. O Christ! To think of the green sea-bottoms and the green-skulled crews! Well, well — maybe the whole world is a ball, as you scholars say, and so it's only right to make one ballroom of it. Dance on, lads — you're young. I was once.
3RD NANTUCKET SAILOR. Break time! Whew! This is harder work than rowing after whales in a calm. Give us a puff, Tash.
(They stop dancing and gather in groups. Meanwhile, the sky darkens — the wind rises.)
LASCAR SAILOR. By Brahma! Boys, it'll be time to take in sail soon. The heaven-born, high-tide Ganges has turned to wind! You show your black brow, Shiva!

MALTESE SAILOR. (Reclining and shaking his cap.) It's the waves — the whitecaps are dancing now. They'll shake their foam-caps soon. If only all the waves were women — then I'd gladly go drown, and dance with them forever! There's nothing so sweet on earth — heaven itself can't match it — as those swift glances from warm, wild women's bosoms in the dance, when their arching arms hide such ripe, bursting grapes.

SICILIAN SAILOR. (Reclining.) Don't tell me about it! Listen, lad — those fleet interlacings of limbs — lithe swayings — flirtings — flutterings! Lip! Heart! Hip! All graze each other: unceasing touch and go! Not a full taste, mind you, or satisfaction would come. Eh, Pagan? (Nudging.)

TAHITIAN SAILOR. (Reclining on a mat.) Hail, holy nakedness of our dancing girls — the Heeva-Heeva! Ah, low-veiled, palm-crowned Tahiti! I still rest on your mat, but the soft earth has shifted! I saw you woven in the forest, my mat! Green the first day I carried you home; now worn and wilted. Ah me! Neither you nor I can bear the change! How would it be, then, if transplanted to that sky? Can I hear the roaring streams from Pirohitee's peak of spears, when they leap down the cliffs and drown the villages? — The blast! The blast! Up, spine, and face it! (Leaps to his feet.)
PORTUGUESE SAILOR. How the sea crashes against the hull! Stand by for reefing, lads! The winds are just crossing swords — soon they'll go lunging at each other.

DANISH SAILOR. Crack, crack, old ship! As long as you're cracking, you're holding! Well done! The mate keeps you to it firmly. He's no more afraid than the island fortress at Kattegat, built to fight the Baltic with storm-battered guns, crusted with sea salt!
4TH NANTUCKET SAILOR. He has his orders, mind you. I heard old Ahab tell him he must always kill a squall, the way you burst a waterspout with a pistol — fire your ship right into it!
ENGLISH SAILOR. Bloody hell, but that old man's a grand old fellow! We're the lads to hunt up his whale!
ALL. Yes! Yes!

OLD MANX SAILOR. How the three masts shake! Pine trees are the hardest to keep alive when transplanted to foreign soil, and here there's none but the crew's cursed clay. Steady, helmsman! Steady. This is the sort of weather when brave hearts break on shore, and hulls split at sea. Our captain has his birthmark. Look there, boys — there's another one in the sky — glowing like that, see? Everything else pitch black.
DAGGOO. What of that? Whoever's afraid of black is afraid of me! I'm carved out of it!

SPANISH SAILOR. (Aside.) He wants a fight, does he? The old grudge makes me touchy. (Stepping forward.) Yes, harpooner, your race is the undeniable dark side of mankind — devilishly dark, at that. No offense.
DAGGOO. (Grimly.) None.
ST. JAGO'S SAILOR. That Spaniard is either mad or drunk. But it can't be drink, or else our old sultan's liquor takes a long time to work in his case.
5TH NANTUCKET SAILOR. What's that I see — lightning? Yes.
SPANISH SAILOR. No. Daggoo showing his teeth.
DAGGOO. (Springing forward.) Swallow yours, runt! White skin, white liver!
SPANISH SAILOR. (Meeting him.) I'll carve you up! Big body, small soul!
ALL. A fight! A fight! A fight!
TASHTEGO. (Taking a puff.) A fight below and a fight aloft — gods and men, both brawlers! Humph!
BELFAST SAILOR. A fight! Arrah, a fight! The Virgin be blessed, a fight! Dive right in!
ENGLISH SAILOR. Fair play! Grab the Spaniard's knife! Make a ring, a ring!
OLD MANX SAILOR. Already formed — look! The ringed horizon. In that ring, Cain struck Abel. Sweet work, proper work! No? Then why, God, did you make the ring?
MATE'S VOICE FROM THE QUARTER-DECK. Hands to the halyards! Take in topgallant sails! Stand by to reef topsails!
ALL. The squall! The squall! Jump, lads! (They scatter.)

PIP. (Shrinking under the windlass.) Lads? Lord help such lads! Crash, smash! There goes the jib-stay! Bang-whang! God! Duck lower, Pip — here comes the royal yard! It's worse than being in the whirling woods on the last day of the year! Who'd go climbing after chestnuts now? But there they go, all cursing, and here I don't. Fine prospects for them — they're on the road to heaven. Hold on tight! Lord, what a squall! But those fellows up there are worse than any storm — they're your white squalls, they are. White squalls? White whale, shh! Shh! Here I've heard all their talk just now, and the white whale — shh! Shh! — mentioned only once! And only this evening — it makes me jingle all over like my tambourine — that snake of an old man swore them all in to hunt it! Oh, great white God up there somewhere in the darkness, have mercy on this small black boy down here. Protect him from all men who have no hearts to feel fear!
